SECTION 1 - NOTE FROM STAFF
Correspondence that required a note from staff. Legislative Services will respond to the writers listed in this section providing the information noted or forthcoming.
1.1
Clayton Greenwood - Pender St. Traffic Calming Measures
1.
Clayton Greenwood - Pender St. Traffic Calming Measures.pdf
Copy: Chief Administrative Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager Community Safety, General Manager Engineering
Note from Legislative Services
: A total of 37 additional names and addresses were received in support of the correspondence. As a privacy statement was not included, the names and addresses have been redacted from the public record.
Note from General Manager Engineering
: The Pender Street and MacDonald Avenue intersection is controlled by an all-way stop, requiring drivers to come to a complete stop before proceeding. The adjacent intersections on Pender Street are also all-way stops, maintaining driver expectations along the corridor. With regards to the recent incident, RCMP is still investigating – the driver was in non-compliance with the stop signs.
Consistent with the Burnaby Transportation Plan's emphasis on road safety, staff will review the traffic calming petition and work with the RCMP for enforcement on stop sign compliance and speeding.
It is to be noted that at the City Council meeting on August 25, 2026, Council adopted the following motion:
THAT
staff provide a report of actions to be taken responding to issues raised by the residents and petitioners for safer streets in the Heights.
1.2
Helen Luketic - Noise or Sound Abatement Bylaw Review
1.
Helen Luketic - Noise or Sound Abatement Bylaw Review.pdf
Copy: Chief Administrative Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager Engineering, General Manager Community Safety
Note from General Manager Community Safety:
Staff have connected with the writer to provide the following information:
The Burnaby Noise or Sound Abatement Bylaw 1979 is currently under review and will include examining bylaws in neighbouring communities.
The noise bylaw in relation to moving vehicle enforcement is available to be used by the RCMP, however, in practice provisions of the
Motor Vehicle Act
are more often utilized by the RCMP.
Bylaw Officers with the City of Burnaby are not trained or authorized to safely stop moving vehicles and there are no plans to have them conduct this work as it is more appropriately performed by the RCMP.
Key arterial routes within the City including Willingdon Ave are intended to support the efficient movement of general traffic, goods and emergency vehicles.  As a result, traditional traffic calming measures are generally not implemented on these routes. Staff will review regulatory signage to reinforce the 50 km/h speed limit and work with the RCMP on enforcement efforts.
Staff will assess the viability of a no U-turn sign at Dawson Street and Willingdon Ave. Under the
Motor Vehicle Act
U-turns are prohibited unless expressly permitted by signage.
Acoustical studies prepared by a professional acoustical engineer are required for most residential rezoning applications including those along major arterial and collector routes.
All new multi-family residential buildings are required to provide cooling in accordance with the
BC Building Code
. Current energy requirements also necessitate the installation of Heat Recovery Ventilators and Energy Recovery Ventilators.
The City does not consider it appropriate to restrict all balconies and operable windows in areas affected by higher traffic noise.
1.3
Maureen Boyd - Washrooms Closed at Madison Square
1.
Maureen Boyd - Washrooms Closed at Madison Square.pdf
Copy: Chief Administrative Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager Planning and Development, General Manager Community Safety
Note from General Manager Community Safety:
Staff will be connecting with the correspondent Maureen Boyd.  While the City of Burnaby does not have a bylaw specific to this issue, our business licences dictate that every holder of a business licence shall comply at all times with every City bylaw or enactment of the Province.  As such, they are subject to the
BC Building Code
which does require businesses to operate washrooms to various specifications based upon occupancy and the expected public use of the space. Inquiries with the property manager have indicated that the washrooms have been shut down due to significant unsanitary behaviour by unknown individuals that included the smearing of feces on the walls of the washroom. Staff will work with the business representative to identify an alternative solution to shutting down the washrooms.
1.4
Paid Parking Expansion in Lake City and Production Way Area
Copy: Chief Administrative Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager Engineering
Note from General Manager
Engineering
:
Burnaby’s Transportation Plan supports sustainable, multi-modal travel by prioritizing walking, cycling, and transit to advance climate, safety, and multi-modal travel goals. The area of Lake City Way and Production Way–University SkyTrain stations have high demands for long-term parking. Staff will monitor parking demand and travel patterns following implementation and assess whether future adjustments are required.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider Pender St. traffic calming review and RCMP enforcement
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a review of traffic calming measures on Pender Street in the Heights neighbourhood, following a petition from residents. The petition was submitted after a recent incident at the Pender Street and MacDonald Avenue intersection, where a driver failed to stop at an all-way stop sign. RCMP is still investigating that incident. City staff will review the petition and work with the RCMP on enforcing stop sign compliance and speeding. This follows a motion adopted by Council on August 25, 2026, directing staff to report on actions to address resident concerns about street safety in the Heights. No new rules have been approved yet — this is a proposed next step.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the upcoming staff report and any public consultation on traffic calming changes for Pender Street in the Heights.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby noise bylaw review and Willingdon traffic measures
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider reviewing the 1979 Noise or Sound Abatement Bylaw, which could change rules for vehicle noise and new buildings. The current bylaw sets penalties of $200 for vehicles exceeding allowable noise and $300 for motorcycles over 80 dBA, though staff note City officers cannot enforce moving violations. Council will also consider signage to reinforce the 50 km/h limit on Willingdon Avenue and a no U-turn sign at Dawson Street. New multi-family buildings must already meet cooling and ventilation standards under the BC Building Code.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on the noise bylaw review—this could affect your property or business operations.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider: Madison Square washroom closures and business licence rules
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a complaint about public washrooms being closed at Madison Square, 4399 Lougheed Hwy, including at Winners. City staff report the washrooms were shut down due to unsanitary behaviour, including feces smeared on walls, and have been closed for about 6 months. While Burnaby has no specific bylaw on washroom access, business licence holders must follow the BC Building Code, which requires washrooms based on occupancy and public use. Staff plan to work with the property manager to find an alternative to keeping the washrooms closed. This is a proposed approach, not a final decision.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you operate a business with public washrooms in Burnaby, watch for updates—this could affect how the city enforces washroom requirements.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider paid parking expansion in Production Way area
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a proposal to expand paid parking in the Production Way and Lake City areas, introducing a city-wide rate of $4 per hour and $10 per day. The proposal would extend paid parking into evenings and weekends, when current free-parking utilization is only 5% to 60%. The submitter questions whether these rates reflect local demand, noting nearby alternatives like TransLink park-and-ride facilities charge $2 to $3 per day. Council has not yet decided, and rates and boundaries remain under consideration.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision and any public consultation on the proposed paid parking expansion in the Production Way and Lake City areas.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider sidewalks on Alaska, Rosser, Juneau streets
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider a renewed request from resident Helen Luketic for sidewalks on Alaska Street, Rosser Avenue, and Juneau Street. This is her third written request since 2022; no sidewalk has been built in four years despite a 2022 commitment to deliver one via the rezoning at 4410 Juneau Street. The corridor serves over 644 occupied homes and is the route to Kitchener Elementary. The request has been referred to the Transportation Committee for review. No decision or construction has been approved yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: If you own property or a business on these streets, watch for public consultation notices and consider contacting the Transportation Committee to share your views.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: New Westminster to tie housing targets to infrastructure funding
agenda_briefs.summary: New Westminster City Council passed a resolution on May 25, 2026, to send letters to Premier Eby, Minister of Housing Christine Boyle, and three MLAs advocating that provincial legislation requiring housing targets or density be directly tied to infrastructure funding. The city argues that current funding tools (Amenity Cost Charges and Development Cost Charges) are insufficient to support growth without making development unviable. The letters also call for provincial services like schools, transit, and affordable housing to keep pace with growth, and a UBCM resolution has been submitted.
agenda_briefs.action_required: No action required; monitor for provincial response to the city's request.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider letter on North Shore wastewater plant review
agenda_briefs.summary: West Vancouver Council is set to consider sending a letter to the Inspector of Municipalities requesting a review under Section 765 of the Local Government Act of the North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant project. The project was originally budgeted at approximately $700 million with a 2020 completion date, and is now projected to be completed in 2030 at an estimated cost of approximately $3.86 billion. The letter would endorse unanimous requests from the City of North Vancouver, District of North Vancouver, and City of New Westminster, and would ask the Inspector to examine factors contributing to cost increases and delays, and provide recommendations to strengthen governance, transparency, accountability, financial oversight, and public confidence in major regional infrastructure projects. The decision is scheduled for an upcoming council meeting and has not yet been finalized.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Attend the council meeting or submit comments to express your views on the proposed letter before the vote.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider impact of new multi-unit developments in Burnaby
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a resident's report on the neighbourhood impact of new multi-unit developments in established single-family areas. The report asks Council to review whether current policies sufficiently require meaningful landscaping and tree planting, green and privacy buffers, building massing and setbacks, and on-site parking that accounts for cumulative street-parking demand as multiple developments cluster in one area. No specific changes are proposed yet — Council will review the findings and decide on next steps, which could shape future rules for developers, property owners, and landlords.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the Council discussion and any follow-up reports — this could lead to new landscaping, setback, and parking rules for multi-unit properties in Burnaby.

agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to consider correspondence from residents Iain Macanulty and Vibeke Rasmussen regarding gas-powered gardening equipment. The item has been referred to senior staff, including the Chief Administrative Officer and General Managers of Engineering, Parks, and Lands, for review. A proposed change could restrict or regulate the use of gas-powered lawn mowers, leaf blowers, and similar equipment in the city. No decision has been made yet — this is an early step in the process. If adopted, a new bylaw could affect landscaping, gardening, and property maintenance practices for businesses and residents.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider: Cohesive bike lane network request
agenda_briefs.summary: Council is set to consider a request from Markus Lau for a cohesive bike lane network in Burnaby. The request, referred to the Chief Administrative Officer, General Manager of Corporate Services, and General Manager of Engineering for review, asks the City to follow Translink's rapid implementation design guide to bridge gaps between developer-built protected bike lanes and the existing network. Examples of disconnected lanes include Imperial St. near Marlborough Ave, Austin Rd. near North Road, and Willingdon Ave. near Beresford and Juneau Sts. If approved, this could affect businesses near current or future bike lanes through changes to parking, deliveries, and customer access. No decision has been made yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for council's decision and any public consultation on bike lane changes that could affect access to your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider urgent primary-care capacity concern from Old Orchard Medical Clinic
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider an urgent primary-care capacity concern from Old Orchard Medical Clinic, which has served Burnaby since 1993. The clinic has shortened weekend hours and reduced evening shifts due to a physician shortage, despite having rooms, staff, EMR and patient demand for more care. It is seeking provincial approval for a Primary Care Network nurse practitioner contract; the Burnaby Division of Family Practice has agreed to submit an MRP request to the Ministry of Health, but approval is not guaranteed and there is no predictable timeline. The clinic warns its long-term financial sustainability may be at risk without more providers, and asks the mayor to write to the Minister of Health, request a Burnaby capacity plan from the Province and Fraser Health, and support a meeting with the City, Fraser Health, the Division and community clinics. No decision has been made.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on this item — it could affect primary-care capacity and related business operations in Burnaby.

agenda_briefs.title: Council to consider chemical-induced wildfires correspondence
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider correspondence from S. Troy Anderson urging BC municipalities to demand a moratorium on chemical climate experimentation (geoengineering), which the letter links to exploding wildfires. The letter cites flammable chemicals in atmospheric spraying and notes Canada lacks domestic laws prohibiting such experiments. This is a proposed item for council's consideration, not a final decision. The outcome could lead to future discussions or actions on wildfire prevention and chemical use, potentially affecting businesses in wildfire-risk areas.

agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will review a formal objection from resident Lydia Ho regarding Muse Cannabis Store at 138-7155 Kingsway (LLA #25-11). Council passed Resolution 2025-408 on August 26, 2025, recommending a provincial retail cannabis licence. City consultation recorded 36 responses: 27 concerns (75%) and 9 in support. The storefront now displays 'COMING SOON' signage. Ms. Ho demands written answers on whether the provincial licence, City business licence, building permits, and inspections are complete, and what authority remains to withhold approvals before opening.
